title_candidates: Cheap AI tokens can hide a risky relay
Check where your discounted AI access really goes
summary: Deeply discounted AI access may route prompts through pooled or compromised accounts. A 15-minute endpoint and usage check can reveal whether your app talks to an official provider.

primary_source.title: An Inside Look at the Relay Market Powering Token Resellers and Fraud
primary_source.author: Matt Lenhard
key_facts: Relay services proxy requests to major AI models and advertise access far below official prices; Vectoral observed discounts as high as 97.8%.
The investigated market has four overlapping layers: card and account sellers, account pools, customer-facing relays, and buyers.
Account pools combine many credentials and rotate around rate limits or disabled accounts while exposing one API to downstream relays.
Many observed relays used open-source gateways that imitate OpenAI's API format and route requests through pooled provider keys.
The gateway software also has legitimate uses; abuse comes from stolen, leaked, fraudulently funded, or terms-violating credentials.
Reported sourcing methods include mass free-trial creation, chargebacks, stolen or prepaid cards, and poorly protected support chatbots.
Vectoral estimated about 3.6 million monthly visits across the ten most-visited relays it tracked.

quote_candidates.text: There’s nothing inherently illicit about the software. one-api and new-api are neutral, legitimate tools.

supporting_sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
key_facts: OpenAI's business terms prohibit buying, selling, or transferring API keys and reselling or leasing account access.

supporting_sources.title: Best Practices for API Key Safety
key_facts: OpenAI advises users not to share API keys and to rotate a key immediately if it may have leaked.

prerequisites: Access to your official AI provider account
Access to the AI app's provider settings

steps.instruction: Open your provider account directly at platform.openai.com or console.anthropic.com, then confirm that the organization, billing details, and API keys are ones you recognize.

In the AI app's provider settings, check the API base URL. Official OpenAI traffic uses api.openai.com and Anthropic traffic uses api.anthropic.com. Stop before entering a key if you see an unfamiliar relay or seller domain.
Open the official provider's usage page and compare recent models, timestamps, and spending with your own activity. Treat unexplained use as a possible compromise.

Copy the current app settings somewhere private, remove the API key from that app only, and send the non-sensitive prompt Reply with SAFE TEST only. The request should fail without a credential; restore it only after the endpoint is trusted.

If anything is suspicious, create a replacement key in the official console, update only trusted apps, revoke the old key, and recheck usage. Never send the replacement through chat, email, or a reseller form.
